overview: This Senate resolution supports naming September 18, 2026, as "National Concussion Awareness Day." A concussion is a mild traumatic brain injury, often caused by a blow to the head in sports, falls or accidents. The resolution cites federal health data showing that millions of such injuries happen each year, many among children and teens, and that many go untreated. It encourages federal, state and local officials to raise awareness and improve diagnosis and treatment of concussions, and supports more research and prevention. It does not create a program or spend money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 23, 2026.
for: Supporters say greater awareness helps parents, coaches and athletes recognize concussions and get proper care, reducing long-term harm.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not fund research or set any new safety rules for youth sports.
